text: al vascular disor- ders. Many species of the genus Senecio, which includes the ragworts and groundsels, are poisonous. They have been found to contain pyrrolizidine alkaloids, which produce hepatic necrosis. The rag- wort, S. jacobaea, which is abundant throughout the British Isles, is poisonous to livestock when eaten in quantity. Poisoning has also been reported in humans after ingestion of herbal teas con- taining pyrrolizidine alkaloids. In the UK, the sale, supply, or im- portation of unlicensed medicinal products containing Senecio spp. for internal use is prohibited. Homoeopathy. Golden ragwort has been used in homoeopath- ic medicines under the following names: Senecio aur.; Senecio aureus; Sen. aur.. Profile Senicapoc is an inhibitor of the Gardos calcium-activated potas- sium channel. It has been investigated to prevent the dehydration of red cells in sickle-cell anaemia. Senlizumab (BAN) Bay-10-3356; Bay-w-3356; CDP-571. Сенлизумаб CAS — 336128-48-4. Profile Senlizumab is a humanised monoclonal antibody to tumour necrosis factor.
